source: JPL Horizons (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/), web form, by hand
licence: None stated by NASA for Horizons; committed with attribution (B.17)
frame: ICRF; positions relative to each segment's centre
units: km, km/s; time ET (TDB seconds past J2000)
interpolation: Hermite through W states (SPK type 13); W per segment in the .bin

-170.name: James Webb Space Telescope
-170.fitQuote: Concatenation of reconstructed trajectory solutions (as-flown) from Goddard Flight Dynamics Facility (FDF), based on tracking data through September 27, with prediction thereafter.

-21.name: SOHO
notes: For the time-span 1998-Aug-19 to 1998-Sep-25, there is no official trajectory information due to the recovery effort. [...] Trajectory errors during this interval may be significant due to unmodeled dynamics.

-78.name: DSCOVR
-78.fitQuote: Concatenated trajectories based on weekly tag-up solutions through 2026-Sep-27, with a short-term prediction extending over the next three weeks.

-85.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
-85.fitQuote: Final reconstructed trajectory segments are from PDS. Preliminary "tag-up" solutions begin 2026-Mar-15, with prediction after 2026-Sep-02.

-152.name: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter
-152.fitQuote: This is a merge of post-launch trajectory solutions fit to tracking data through 2026-Sep-29, with a prediction thereafter.

-1024.name: Artemis II (Orion Integrity)
-1024.fitQuote: Post-launch Orion II trajectory data from NASA/JSC navigation (concatenated).
notes: The data sheet does not say which segments are reconstructions. It was revised after splashdown (2026-Apr-11 00:07 UTC).

-31.name: Voyager 1
notes: #1) 1977-Sep-5 to 1981-Jan-1: A patched conic mission-design type trajectory in which the conics were constructed to approximately match specific events, such as satellite encounters, providing a rough accuracy.

#2) 1981-Jan-1 to 2100-Jan-1 Refit of tracking data spanning 1981-1992 (end of two-way coherent transponder data). Done in 2022 by R. Jacobson (former Voyager navigation) using DE440 to generate a new solution and prediction.
Formal predicted geocentric pointing uncertainty on 2030-Jan-1: RA +/- 1.701 arcseconds, DEC +/- 1.535 arcseconds

-32.name: Voyager 2
notes: The timeline says "1992-Jul-17 Last transponder tracking data"; the tracking-data table's last point, used here, is 30-Oct-1992.

#1) 1977-Aug-20 to 1989-Aug-29: A patched conic mission-design type trajectory in which the conics were constructed to approximately match specific events (such satellite encounters), providing a rough accuracy.
Formal predicted geocentric pointing uncertainty on 2030-Jan-1: RA +/- 4.718 arcseconds, DEC +/- 3.715 arcseconds

-23.name: Pioneer 10
-23.lastContactQuote: The last fully successful acquisition of signal was March 3, 2002.
notes: NOTE: This trajectory is suitable for general historical purposes, but should be used cautiously for high precision or tracking data applications.

-24.name: Pioneer 11
-24.lastContactQuote: Science operations and daily telemetry ceased on September 30, 1995 when the RTG power level was insufficient to operate any experiments.
notes: NOTE: This trajectory is suitable for general historical purposes, but should be used cautiously for high precision or tracking data applications.

-98.name: New Horizons
-98.fitQuote: Concatenated spacecraft trajectory (from NH navigation, KinetX, tracking data cut-off July 20, 2026 19:11:55 TDB).

-82.name: Cassini
-82.fitQuote: UPDATED with "final" post-mission reconstruction, 2004 to end-of-mission.
notes: Before 2004 the data sheet says only: "Trajectories provided by the Navigation Team (concatenated here)."

-77.name: Galileo
-77.fitQuote: Trajectory provided by Navigation Team (JPL). Data fit: 1989 to Aug 12, 2002, baseline predicts thereafter.

-61.name: Juno
-61.fitQuote: The trajectory after 2026-Sep-23 is a planning prediction.

-159.name: Europa Clipper
-159.fitQuote: Segments marked by '*' below are pre-launch predictions. Then based on tracking data through 2026-Sep-22. Trajectory thereafter is predicted

-28.name: JUICE
-28.fitQuote: Post-launch trajectory from ESA based on tracking data through September 22, prediction after that.

-96.name: Parker Solar Probe
-96.fitQuote: Fit to post-launch tracking data through 2026-Sep-01. Reference planning trajectory for subsequent times.

-121.name: BepiColombo
-121.fitQuote: Trajectory from ESA. Data fit through 2026-Sep-28, prediction thereafter.

-255.name: Psyche
-255.fitQuote: Post-launch spacecraft trajectory from JPL navigation. Data through August 11, prediction thereafter.

-64.name: OSIRIS-REx / OSIRIS-APEX
notes: The data sheet states no fit boundary.

-74.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
-74.fitQuote: Trajectory after 2026-Sep-27 is a planning PREDICTION.

-202.name: MAVEN
-202.fitQuote: Fit to data through 2025-Dec-04, prediction thereafter.
notes: [...] with some evidence it experienced an unplanned delta-V Dec. 4 and is spinning in an altered trajectory. Therefore predicts after December 4, 2025 may be inaccurate.

-3.name: Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
-3.fitQuote: Merge of DSN/JPL/Nav data-fit tag-up trajectory through April 2022. Prediction thereafter.
notes: The interval from 2019-Oct-01 to 2020-Apr-29 may drift slightly from actual, with discontinuties on 2020-Mar-30 and 2020-Apr-18 when the trajectory was updated from a new initial ISRO state integration, not a new data fit.
